s leaf `--api-key`.

Credential precedence for Cloud commands:

1. `--api-key` — must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key
is a usage error.\n2. `MCPJAM_API_KEY` — same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in this env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval
reporting can still use it.\n3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`\n4. Missing — Cloud commands fail with login guidance befor

e they hit the network (`mcpjam cloud status` reports `missing` instead)

API URL precedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_
URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same server without `/api/v1`)\n3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is
the credential; a login saved before logins recorded their server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a u

sable address is refused with exit `3`)
4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`

Every command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `
--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJA
M_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error
(exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does
not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order picks
another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it st
ill emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and
exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credential.valid: null`) and successful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an
audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays

on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.

## Cloud project scope

Most Cloud commands pick one project:

1. `--project <

id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `project` field in `--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJECT`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.js

on`
5. Automatic — the most recently updated project you can see

Empty `--project` or `MCPJAM_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJ
AM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** select a Cloud CLI project (it is SDK eval reporting only).\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-variable

s"}
mcpjam cloud login
mcpjam cloud link # writes .mcpjam/project.json (no secrets)
mcpjam cloud status
# zero-network: credential, deployment, selector\nmcpjam cloud eval list # uses the link\nmcpjam cloud link

--remove
```

`mcpjam cloud eval` run-inspection commands (`status`, `cancel`, `judge`, `iterations`, `gate`, `compare`, `trace
`, `steps`, `screenshot`, `video`) follow the same rule — `--project` is optional. `mcpjam cloud sessions list` does too; `--all-p
rojects` restores a cross-project listing and cannot be combined with `--project`. Hosted `readiness` never reads the project link

.

## What `--host` means

`--host` is not one flag. The meaning depends on the command:

| Where | What it selects |
| - |
- |\n| `server`, `tools`, `resources`, `prompts` | An **AI client** (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `cursor`, …). The CLI sends that host's
`clientInfo`, capabilities, and protocol version in `initialize`. |\n| `test --host` | One host **template** to emulate for a loc
al suite run: its handshake, tool visibility and model settings. Never the real client. |\n| `compat --host` | Which AI clients to
report. Repeatable; default is all. |\n| `cloud eval --host`, `cloud goals`, `cloud studies` | A **saved project Host** (`<id-or-
name>`), the client config an eval or goal run is stamped with. |\n| `cloud environments --host-id` | The project Host id the envi
ronment runs as. Distinct from eval's `--host`. |\n\n`--host` on a local command is mutually exclusive with `--client-capabilities
`. A Cloud `--host` is mutually exclusive with `--server` / `--environment` when those already supply a closed server set.\n\n## G
lobal flags\n\nThese flags apply to every command. Cloud credentials `--api-key` / `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud`, not

the program root.

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--timeout <ms>` | `30000` | Request timeout in milliseco
nds |\n| `--rpc` | off | Include raw JSON-RPC request/response logs in JSON output under `_rpcLogs` |\n| `--quiet` | off | Suppres
s non-result progress output on stderr |\n| `--no-telemetry` | off | Disable anonymous telemetry for this invocation |\n| `--forma
t <format>` | `human` on TTY, `json` when piped | Raw output format (`json` or `human`) |\n| `-v, --version` | | Print the CLI ver

sion |

## Output formats

The CLI auto-detects whether stdout is a terminal:

* **Interactive terminal** — defaults to `--f
ormat human`. For most commands this is pretty-printed JSON; `server doctor` and the OAuth conformance commands provide dedicated
human-readable summaries.\n* **Piped or redirected** (CI, `| jq`, agent invocation) — defaults to `--format json`, the full struct
ured result.\n* **Conformance in CI** — `protocol conformance`, `protocol conformance-suite`, `oauth conformance`, `oauth conforma
nce-suite`, `apps conformance`, and `apps conformance-suite` support `--reporter junit-xml` and `--reporter json-summary`.\n* **Ex
plicit `--format`** always wins over the auto-detected default.\n\n**For agents**: raw JSON is the source of truth. Human format i
s a lossy presentation layer. If you're parsing output programmatically, pass `--quiet --format json`.\n\nJSON-valued flags accept
inline JSON, `@path`, or `-` for stdin. `tools call` also accepts `--tool-args-stdin` as a shorthand for `--tool-args -`. Use fil
lue\"}' | mcpjam tools call --url $URL --access-token $TOKEN \\\n --tool-name my_tool --tool-args - --quiet --format json\n```\n\

n## Connecting to servers

The CLI supports two transport modes, selected by which flags you pass:

* `--url ...` selects HTTP
.\n* `--command ...` selects stdio.\n* `--transport http|stdio` is optional and acts as an explicit override/validator when you wa

nt the CLI to reject mismatched flags early.

### HTTP (Streamable HTTP / SSE)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
m

cpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp
```

Add auth when needed:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}

# Static bearer token
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN

# OAuth tokens from a pri

or login
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --oauth-access-token $TOKEN

# Custom headers
mcpjam server do

ctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --header "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

### Stdio (local subprocess)

```bash theme={"theme

":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server doctor --command node --args server.js --cwd /path/to/project -e API_KEY=[REDACTED]
```

S
tdio child processes inherit the parent shell environment by default. Use\n`-e/--env` to add values or override inherited ones for
the spawned server.\nStructured debug artifacts only record the explicit env keys you pass through\n`-e/--env`; inherited shell v

ariables are not enumerated.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `oauth ...` and `protocol ...` are HTTP-only command groups. They do
> not accept

stdio targets.

## Update notifications

After a successful command, the CLI checks whether a newer version of `@mcpjam/cli`

is available and prints a notice to stderr when one is found:

```
Update available: @mcpjam/cli 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0
Run npm instal

l -g @mcpjam/cli to update
```

The check is non-blocking: version data is fetched in a detached background process and cached
locally for 24 hours, so it never slows down your commands. The notice is written to stderr only and never touches stdout or JSON
output, so it is safe for both interactive terminals and AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) that capture stderr. It is suppress

ed automatically in CI.

To opt out, set one of these environment variables before running any command:

| Variable | Effect |

| - | - |
| `MCPJAM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` | Disable update checks for `@mcpjam/cli` |
| `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` | Disable update c
